question: Should memory-wiki vault isolation be solved through generic `agents.list[].plugins` overrides, a memory-wiki-owned per-agent/workspace vault resolver, or an explicit unsupported/shared-gateway limitation?
rationale: Automation cannot safely choose the permanent config, SecretRef, lifecycle, CLI/gateway, and upgrade semantics for a security-sensitive cross-agent memory boundary.

options.title: Design generic agent-scoped plugin config
options.body: Add a shared per-agent plugin config contract with precedence, SecretRef/redaction, schema validation, restart semantics, docs, and memory-wiki coverage built on that contract.

options.title: Add memory-wiki-owned vault scoping only
options.body: Keep global plugin config but give memory-wiki an explicit per-agent/workspace vault mapping or resolver, reducing generic core surface while creating plugin-specific semantics.

options.title: Document shared-vault limitation for now
options.body: State that memory-wiki is not isolated across agents on one gateway and require separate gateways or disabled memory-wiki until a broader design lands.

recommendation.title: Design generic agent-scoped plugin config
recommendation.body: Add a shared per-agent plugin config contract with precedence, SecretRef/redaction, schema validation, restart semantics, docs, and memory-wiki coverage built on that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans plugin config runtime, SDK/config compatibility, security semantics, and recent memory-wiki state work where steipete has the strongest current boundary history.
